'''Claus Jönsson''' (26 May 1930 – 25 August 2024) was a German [[Applied physics|applied physicist]] who specialized in [[Electron microscope|electron microscopy]].<ref name=":0">{{cite news |year=2024 |title=Er führte das schönste physikalische Experiment aller Zeiten in Tübingen durch: Zum Tode von Professor Dr. Claus Jönsson ein Nachruf von Amand Faessler |trans-title=He carried out the most beautiful physics experiment of all time in Tübingen |url=https://uni-tuebingen.de/universitaet/aktuelles-und-publikationen/newsletter-uni-tuebingen-aktuell/2024/4/leute/4/ |work=Eberhard Karls Universität Tübingen |language=de}}</ref>

==Life==
Jönsson was born in [[Charlottenburg|Charlottenberg]], Berlin, Germany in 1930 and grew up near Hamburg. He matriculated at the [[University of Tübingen]] to study physics in 1953. Due to a critical shortage of student housing, he had to rent a space 12 km away.<ref name=":0" />
[[File:Claus Jönsson Interferenz.jpg|left|thumb|The interference fringes of electrons from Jönsson's experiment of 1959]]
Jönsson came under the tutelage of [[Gottfried Möllenstedt]], the "German pope" of electron microscopy.<ref name=":0" /> In 1961, Jönsson published the results of his [[double-slit experiment]] performed with beams of [[electrons]],<ref>Jönsson C, (1961) ''Zeitschrift für Physik'', '''161''':454–474 {{doi|10.1007/BF01342460}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite journal | last1 = Jönsson | first1 = C | year = 1974 | title = Electron diffraction at multiple slits | journal = American Journal of Physics | volume = 42 | pages = 4–11 | doi = 10.1119/1.1987592 |bibcode = 1974AmJPh..42....4J }}</ref> something previously thought to be unfeasible in practice.<ref name=":0" /> Jönsson conducted his experiment in 1959 for his doctoral dissertation at Tübingen, working late at night.<ref name=":0" /> He discovered how to focus a narrow beam of electrons traveling towards the slits, resulting in the familiar [[Wave interference|interference pattern]].<ref name=":0" /> He observed interference fringes for up to five slits.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Tonomura |first=Akira |date=September 1, 2002 |title=The double-slit experiment |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/the-double-slit-experiment/ |access-date=June 16, 2025 |website=Physics World}}</ref> Jönsson's original paper was published in English for the first time in 1974 on the ''[[American Journal of Physics]]''.<ref name=":1" /> The journal's editors, [[Anthony French]] and [[Edwin F. Taylor|Edwin Taylor]], praised the experiment as "great" but noted that "pedagogically clean fundamental experiments" such as this one would likely not bring professional fame.<ref name=":2" /> Indeed, Jönsson's experiment had been largely unknown and the double-slit experiment for electrons (and other quantum objects) was typically presented as a [[thought experiment]].<ref name=":2" /> More advanced versions of Jönsson's experiment were subsequently performed, including with individual electrons being sent towards the slits.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rosa |first1=Rodolfo |year=2012 |title=The Merli–Missiroli–Pozzi Two-Slit Electron-Interference Experiment |journal=Physics in Perspective |volume=14 |issue=2 |pages=178–194 |bibcode=2012PhP....14..178R |doi=10.1007/s00016-011-0079-0 |pmc=4617474 |pmid=26525832}}</ref>

Even so, in 2002, Jönsson's work was named "the most beautiful experiment" by readers of ''[[Physics World]]''.<ref name="r3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20160304093731/http://www.uni-protokolle.de/nachrichten/id/6681/ Schönstes physikalisches Experiment aller Zeiten in Tübingen durchgeführt]. Eberhard-Karls-Universität Tübingen. 25 September 2002</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Crease |first=Robert P. |author-link=Robert P. Crease |date=September 15, 2002 |title=The most beautiful experiments in physics as chosen by real physicists |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/the-most-beautiful-experiments-in-physics-as-chosen-by-real-physicists/ |access-date=June 16, 2025 |work=Physics World}}</ref>

He served as a professor at the Institute for Applied Physics at Tübingen from 1978 to his retirement in 1995.<ref>{{Cite news |last=University of Tübingen |title=Fachbereich Physik: Trauer um Herrn Prof. Dr. Claus Jönsson |trans-title=Department of Physics: In the Memory of Prof. Dr. Claus Jönsson |url=https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/mathematisch-naturwissenschaftliche-fakultaet/fakultaet/aktuelles/news-aus-der-fakultaet/newsfullview-fakultaet/article/fachbereich-physik-trauer-um-herrn-prof-dr-claus-joensson/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926213110/https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/mathematisch-naturwissenschaftliche-fakultaet/fakultaet/aktuelles/news-aus-der-fakultaet/newsfullview-fakultaet/article/fachbereich-physik-trauer-um-herrn-prof-dr-claus-joensson/ |archive-date=September 26, 2024 |access-date=June 16, 2025 |department=Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences |language=German}}</ref>
